description: Things the jabberwock was taught, filed under 'spatial_exploration'. Written by the teach() facility (one node per taught item).

attrs.answer: Treat UNKNOWN space as FREE: plan the shortest path through it as if traversable, mark a cell blocked ONLY when an observation refutes it, then replan. Named the 'freespace assumption' (Koenig & Smirnov 1997) / 'optimistic policy under uncertainty' (Canadian Traveller Problem). On a grid this is the established, near-optimal standard: the planned path is a lower bound on true cost and you never abandon a route until physically disproven. The PESSIMISTIC opposite — only trust cells you have actually traversed (confirm-before-trust) — FAILS: when every route to a goal crosses unknown cells (the normal start condition) it sees no connected path, only nibbles the frontier, and produces far worse coverage.

A FRONTIER is a known-FREE cell adjacent to at least one UNKNOWN cell — the boundary between mapped and uncharted space (Yamauchi 1997). Always drive to the NEAREST REACHABLE frontier, distance measured as true grid PATH length not Euclidean. This is provably COMPLETE: eliminating every reachable frontier <=> covering all reachable space, because any path to unknown space must cross a frontier. Cluster adjacent frontier cells into regions, drop sub-agent-size clusters, target the region centroid.

Rank frontiers by ACTUAL shortest-path travel cost from the agent, NOT straight-line distance (Euclidean scoring lures the agent into wall-blocked dead-ends). One goal-rooted wavefront/Dijkstra flood from the agent's pose yields the cost-to-every-frontier field in a single pass — reuse it as BOTH the selection utility AND the navigation gradient (steepest descent).

OSCILLATION/thrashing between two near-equidistant frontiers happens when you re-pick the target every tick by argmax: a tiny map update flips the winner and the agent reverses without advancing either. FIX: COMMIT with hysteresis — lock onto the chosen frontier until it is REACHED, INVALIDATED, or a fixed fraction (e.g. half) of the path is traversed; only THEN re-evaluate. Never reselect on a per-tick argmax over near-tied scores. This is the direct cure for the avatar bouncing between two cells.

Keep a PERSISTENT GLOBAL frontier list, not just locally-visible frontiers. Greedy local-only tracking FORGETS isolated unexplored pockets and forces long backtracks (this is the 'corridor boxing' trap). A global list guarantees completeness (no pocket forgotten); utility ordering handles efficiency. When the nearest frontier is unreachable/abandoned, the agent should route to the next-best GLOBAL frontier, possibly backtracking through known space to reach it from a different side.

On each obstacle discovery only ~15% of cells' goal-distances change. REPAIR only the locally-inconsistent region (LPA* / D* Lite, Koenig & Likhachev) instead of replanning from scratch — 1-2 orders of magnitude faster. Root cost-to-go values at the GOAL (search goal->start) so they survive agent motion; a node is locally inconsistent iff g != rhs (one-step lookahead); the priority queue holds exactly those nodes.

When the optimistic planner STALLS or oscillates, fall back to a local-sensing WALL-FOLLOWING traversal that is provably COMPLETE and path-bounded. Bug2 (Lumelsky & Stepanov 1987): follow the straight start->goal m-line; on hitting an obstacle, wall-follow it; leave only when re-crossing the m-line CLOSER to the goal than where you hit it. The bare right-hand rule alone is complete ONLY on loop-free spaces; Tremaux's algorithm (mark passages, prefer unmarked, never re-enter a twice-marked passage) handles looped mazes. The m-line / progress condition is what stops the agent circling forever.

To upgrade nearest-frontier, pick argmax U(v) = I(v) * exp(-lambda * cost(agent,v)), where I(v) is the EXPECTED INFORMATION GAIN (entropy reduction) of going there — estimated cheaply by ray-casting how many unknown cells would be revealed. Per-cell occupancy entropy is maximal at p=0.5 (unknown), zero when known. Nearest-frontier is the special case I=const. Reward expected LEARNING PROGRESS, not raw novelty (pure novelty stalls on high-entropy-but-unlearnable regions — the 'noisy-TV problem').

Humans bootstrap a new space in layers: WALL-FOLLOWING (thigmotaxis) as a cheap ORIENTATION prior before any model exists, biasing toward openings/doorways, THEN hand off to frontier/info-gain seeking. Spatial knowledge develops landmark -> route -> survey (Siegel & White): anchor salient landmarks, chain them into routes as you traverse, fold overlapping routes into an allocentric SURVEY map that supports novel shortcuts. Map, don't log: store configurational/allocentric structure, not a list of steps.

Humans CHUNK space into nested regions (rooms/districts) and plan COARSE-THEN-FINE: pick the region sequence first, then the within-region route — cheaper than flat search and resists getting lost. Local vs global search uses the cheap AREA-RESTRICTED-SEARCH control law (Charnov's Marginal Value Theorem): on a find, turn more / step less (search locally); on a miss-streak, straighten / step more (travel); LEAVE a region when its local discovery rate falls to the running global average. Boundaries, a metric grid, and a heading/compass are first-class map primitives (place/grid/border/head-direction cells).
